On Tue, Nov 21, 2028 at 11:12 AM Alice Wong <alice@finari.io> wrote:
> We're seeing a sudden jump in p99 latency (from ~420ms to >3s) on our checkout stream ...

I've pulled the pcap and started replaying frames against our local client dechunker / streaming parser. Quick notes (initial triage):
- I can reproduce a high-latency tail when frames from multiple concurrent streams interleave and include header continuation lines across chunk boundaries.
- The client SDK's header reassembly code assumes contiguous header blocks and will occasionally block on waiting for a continuation that arrives later, which stalls processing of subsequent frames.
- This is exacerbated when our CDN/proxy shuffles micro-batches (we get jitter in chunk delivery order).

Short mitigation we can apply server-side: mark affected customer routes to a slightly more conservative framing policy (disable aggressive multiplexing) — that will add ~60ms median but collapse the p99 spike.

I will attach a minimal repro diff (reassembly-unit-test.diff) and a log snippet in the ticket.

Attachments: reassembly-unit-test.diff (patch)

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

Team — thanks Vanessa for the triage. This looks like a client-side reassembly race that only surfaces under framing jitter from proxies/CDNs. Action plan:
1) Immediate: Naomi — please request Finari to apply the temporary route override (we can provide the UI steps). This reduces p99 quickly (target <500ms) and keeps their checkout available.
2) Hotfix: Vanessa to prepare a minimal server-side compatibility toggle and rollout to us-east canaries within 2 hours. If metrics look good we push global.
3) SDK patch: Vanessa will prepare a client SDK patch that treats header continuation as tolerant (non-blocking) — target patch within 48 hours and a patch release.
4) Exec comms: Marissa — can you prepare a one-paragraph incident note for GTM and Sales leadership? We'll escalate to Ops if we see regressions.

I'll own the rollout coordination and metric checks. Naomi, please keep Finari leadership updated.

Rishi Malhotra

Confirming our SDK: finari-js v2.4.1 with Redwood bundled HTTP2 adapter. We saw connection resets in a handful of clients but not consistently.

We accepted the route override and started seeing p99 drop within 5 minutes — thanks. Baseline now sits at ~470ms p99 and spikes are significantly reduced. Still seeing short residual spikes (~1s) every ~20 minutes.

We're on the call now; happy to keep you posted and provide any additional logs.

Alice

Subject: Finari: status update and next steps (post-mitigation)

Alice / team — short update following yesterday's work and today's checks.

Summary:
- Root cause (preliminary): client SDK header reassembly code blocks on continuation lines when frames are delivered out-of-order by aggressive multiplexing/proxy micro-batching. This manifests as p99 tail latency and intermittent timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: route override applied by Finari + conservative server framing policy from our side. Observed p99 improved from >3s spikes to ~450–520ms; throughput normalized.
- Planned next actions:
  * Vanessa to ship server-side compatibility toggle to canaries (in progress, deadline 2028-11-21T14:30Z).
  * SDK patch (non-blocking header continuation) targeted in 48 hours; we'll share a patch and a canary release plan.
  * Postmortem + customer-facing summary to be shared by Friday EOD.

We've opened RI-7342 and attached the artifacts (pcap, p99 CSV, unit-test diff). Marissa is prepping the exec note and I'll coordinate the customer postmortem.

If anything changes in the metrics or if Finari sees a regression, ping me immediately and we'll elevate to SEV.

Thanks for your patience — Naomi
